title: Maharashtra Lets Restaurants Stay Open Until 4 AM for World Cup Final as India Braces for Sunday's Showdown
excerpt: The state government extended operating hours so fans can watch the Argentina-Spain final in restaurants and bars across Mumbai and Maharashtra, following similar moves in other states.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Maharashtra allows restaurants to stay open until 4 AM for the World Cup final.
  • The Argentina-Spain final starts at 12:30 AM IST on July 21.
  • Late-night extensions reflect football's growing popularity in India.
  • The match is expected to be the most-watched football event in India.
  • Previous extensions occurred for major sporting events like the ICC Cricket World Cup.
Maharashtra's Late-Night Football Boost
›Restaurants and bars open until 4 AM on July 20.
›Final match kicks off at 12:30 AM IST.
›Previous late-night extensions for World Cup and Champions League.
›Cultural and commercial opportunity for Mumbai's nightlife.
  • Maharashtra has allowed restaurants and bars to stay open until 4 AM on the night of July 20 so fans can watch the FIFA World Cup final between Argentina and Spain.
  • The Argentina-Spain final kicks off at 12:30 AM IST on Monday, July 21 (4 PM ET on Sunday, July 20), making the extended hours essential for communal viewing.
  • The decision follows similar late-night extensions by state governments for major sporting events in recent years, reflecting football's growing popularity in India.

Late-Night Permission for the Beautiful Game

The Maharashtra government has granted restaurants and bars across the state permission to remain open until 4 AM on the night of Sunday, July 20, so fans can watch the FIFA World Cup final between Argentina and Spain.

The decision addresses the time-zone challenge that has defined India's relationship with global football for decades. The final at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey kicks off at 4 PM Eastern Time — which translates to 12:30 AM India Standard Time on Monday morning. Without extended hours, most restaurants and bars in Mumbai and across Maharashtra would have been required to close well before the match concluded.

Football's Growing Hold on India

The extension reflects the continued growth of football fandom in India, driven by the Premier League's large Indian viewership base, the rise of the Indian Super League, and the global reach of stars like Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo. World Cup viewership in India has climbed steadily, and the 2026 tournament — the first with 48 teams — has drawn particular attention because of the expanded format and the tournament's North American time zones, which are more favorable for Indian viewers than the Qatar 2022 edition's afternoon kickoffs.

The Argentina-Spain final is expected to be the most-watched football match in Indian television history. Argentina's run through the tournament — and the narrative of Messi's likely final World Cup — has built enormous anticipation. The match will also carry a geopolitical undertone, with the Falklands-related banner controversy between Argentina and England during the semifinal still generating discussion.

Precedent and Context

State governments in India have occasionally extended restaurant and bar operating hours for major global sporting events. Similar permissions have been granted during previous World Cup and Champions League finals, as well as ICC Cricket World Cup knockout matches. The extensions are typically issued through the local excise department and apply to licensed establishments.

For Mumbai's vibrant food and nightlife scene, the extended hours represent both a cultural moment and a commercial opportunity. Restaurants and sports bars across the city are advertising screening events, many with World Cup-themed menus and group viewing packages.

How Diaspora Fans Will Watch

For NRIs in the United States, the final falls during comfortable afternoon viewing hours — a rare advantage that has made this World Cup particularly accessible for the Indian diaspora. Many Indian restaurants and community centers across major US cities have organized screening events, creating the kind of communal viewing experience that is difficult to replicate outside a World Cup year. The combination of the time zone and the tournament's physical proximity has made the 2026 edition the most-watched World Cup among Indian Americans, according to early viewership data.
